question: What generation, detection, biometric-security, application, and governance landscape defines face deepfakes, and which gaps prevent dependable defenses?

key_findings.claim: The review organizes face deepfakes by whole-face synthesis, identity swap, attribute manipulation, and expression reenactment, then compares their architectures, losses, and metrics.
key_findings.evidence: Its generation taxonomy separates driving modality and manipulation target and tabulates landmark, autoencoder, GAN, and newer generation families alongside detection cues spanning artifacts, physiology, frequency, and audiovisual consistency.

key_findings.claim: The survey finds no universal detector and identifies cross-generator robustness and inconsistent evaluation as central bottlenecks.
key_findings.evidence: Detection methods frequently exploit artifacts specific to a dataset or generator; the future-work audit calls for generalized and explainable multimodal detectors, shared protocols, identity recovery, and governance.

key_findings.claim: The authors add an empirical biometric attack audit rather than only summarizing literature.
key_findings.evidence: They generate face swaps and reenactments for 36 VoxCeleb2 subjects with five methods, then test five recognition backbones using attack success and cosine similarity at model-specific false-accept thresholds.

method.core_idea: Synthesize an algorithm-centered survey spanning generation, detection, applications, biometric attacks, and policy gaps, supplemented by a controlled face-verification attack study.
method.mechanism: Literature is grouped by manipulation and detection signal; architectures, losses, datasets, and metrics are compared, and selected generators are evaluated against multiple recognition systems.
assumptions: The selected literature and five generators represent the rapidly changing field.
Face-focused image/video deepfakes can be analyzed separately from audio, text, and full-body synthesis.
Attack success on VoxCeleb2 approximates risk to remote biometric verification.

techniques.role: Separates identity, expression, attribute, and whole-face synthesis.
Compares spatial, temporal, physiological, frequency, and multimodal forensic cues.
Crosses multiple generators with multiple face-recognition backbones and thresholds.

evaluations.setting: 36 VoxCeleb2 identities, five synthesis methods, five recognition backbones
evaluations.metric: Attack success rate and cosine similarity at fixed FAR thresholds
evaluations.result: The study shows generator- and recognizer-dependent vulnerability rather than a single universal risk level.
evaluations.baseline: Genuine enrollment/verification behavior and different generator-recognizer pairs

limitations: The survey search and inclusion protocol is not a formal systematic-review pipeline.
Coverage stops before later foundation video generators and provenance standards.
The added biometric audit is small, face-only, and does not reproduce deployment liveness checks.
failure_modes: Artifact detectors fail when compression or a new generator removes their cue.
Single-modality detectors miss cross-modal inconsistency and can be evaded by coordinated synthesis.
Incomparable datasets, thresholds, and metrics create misleading leaderboards.
reusable_insights: Deepfake defense should be evaluated as a generator-by-detector-by-channel matrix.
Biometric risk requires model-specific thresholds rather than raw similarity alone.
Universal detection claims need held-out future generators and post-processing, not only cross-dataset tests.
open_questions: How should evaluation stream unseen generators over time to measure detector decay?
Can content provenance and identity recovery complement statistical detection under adaptive attack?
Which multimodal cues survive coordinated audio-video generation and real platform compression?

competitive_landscape.title: Deepfake Generation and Detection: A Benchmark and Survey
competitive_landscape.difference: Pei et al. provide a benchmark-centered review across four generation fields; this review places more emphasis on algorithmic losses, biometric recognition attacks, applications, and governance.

competitive_landscape.title: Evolving from Single-modal to Multi-modal Facial Deepfake Detection: A Survey
competitive_landscape.difference: Liu et al. center the shift to audiovisual and text-visual detection, while this paper jointly reviews generation and empirically audits face-biometric vulnerability.

competitive_landscape.title: FaceForensics++: Learning to Detect Manipulated Facial Images
competitive_landscape.difference: FaceForensics++ standardizes four manipulation families and compression levels; the review shows how later generation/detection work and biometric threats extend beyond that benchmark.

novelty_assessment: Reviewer inference: many deepfake surveys and benchmarks already exist. The differentiator is breadth across algorithm internals, applications, biometric implications, and policy, plus a multi-generator/multi-recognizer attack audit; it is synthesis rather than a new detector.
reviewer_notes: Full review structure, conclusion, supplementary future directions, and biometric protocol were checked. Statements about universal-detector absence are field-level judgments, not impossibility results. Primary records checked 2026-08-23.
